live_discovery.rule: Use the currently discovered connector actions and schemas. Remembered GitHub REST endpoints or previously available connector functions do not establish current support or authorization.

input_translation: Map canonical repository identity to repo_full_name only after the project/provider binding is resolved.
Map source revision to commit_sha when discovering pull-request-triggered runs for a commit.
Use run_id for run-job inspection and job_id for step/log inspection; keep provider IDs in integration detail rather than domain truth.
output_translation: Normalize observed run/job/step status, attempt identity when available, and evidence references into pipeline execution evidence with provider provenance.
Treat decoded job logs as bounded evidence, not as canonical task state or automatic QA/release proof.
pipeline.inspect.auth_scope: Require live connector read availability for the repository/actions surface. Exact authentication and scope evidence must be discovered; do not infer it from the connected provider name.
pipeline.inspect.availability_discovery: Require all provider actions needed by the requested inspection fidelity to be present in live discovery. Missing actions reduce fidelity to PARTIAL or UNSUPPORTED rather than triggering an unapproved raw-API fallback.
pipeline.inspect.verification: READ operation; preserve provider/source revision and the exact action/result provenance consumed by the domain workflow.
pipeline.inspect.retry_and_reconciliation: Read retries may follow surfaced transient/rate-limit guidance. Do not fabricate provider rate-limit values. A retry must not change semantic scope silently.
limitations: fetch_commit_workflow_runs currently filters to pull-request-triggered runs and returns the first page only.
fetch_workflow_run_jobs returns the latest attempt's jobs from the first page only.
The inspected connector surface does not expose arbitrary historical-run pagination or environment-policy state through this mapping.
Job logs can contain sensitive operational data; retrieve only the bounded job required by the owning workflow.

pipeline.execute.semantic_guard: Map a rerun action to pipeline.execute only when the owning workflow proves the requested job/run is a bounded non-deployment pipeline execution whose declared maximum effect is no stronger than EXTERNAL_WRITE. If the job/run can deploy, perform destructive work, or communicate externally, do not use this mapping; resolve the stronger semantic capability such as deploy.execute or return BLOCKED/UNSUPPORTED.
input_translation: Bind repo_full_name plus run_id or job_id to the canonical project/repository and fixed source/build inputs.
Bind the original run/job identity and observed attempt state before mutation so duplicate prevention and postcondition verification have a fixed point.
output_translation: Record provider acknowledgement separately from observed postcondition state.
After an allowed rerun request, re-read the relevant run/jobs and record the new attempt/observed state before returning APPLIED.
pipeline.execute.auth_scope: The discovered rerun connector actions require GitHub Actions write permission for the repository. That permission is auth/scope evidence only; it never grants operation authority.
pipeline.execute.operation_authority: Require Capability Operation Envelope plus project capability-execution policy verdict before execution. Provider availability or Actions write permission alone never authorizes the rerun.
pipeline.execute.idempotency: A rerun request is not idempotent by repetition. Use the original run/job identity plus observed attempt state as duplicate-prevention evidence; never blindly retry an ambiguous request.
pipeline.execute.retry_and_reconciliation: If the rerun request times out, disconnects, or returns ambiguous provider acknowledgement, re-inspect run/job attempt state before issuing any retry. If consumed state cannot be reconciled, return FAILED/BLOCKED truthfully rather than guessing no execution occurred.
pipeline.execute.postcondition_verification: Provider acknowledgement is not a verified postcondition. APPLIED requires read-after-write evidence that the intended rerun/attempt exists in the consumed provider state.
pipeline.execute.compensation: No truthful rollback can erase a rerun attempt after the provider accepted it. Compensation is UNAVAILABLE unless a distinct authorized semantic operation exists; report the attempted operation truthfully.
pipeline.execute.concurrency: Respect the owning Delivery Pipeline design's concurrency/serialization policy. This mapping does not override provider or project concurrency controls.
limitations: The inspected connector exposes rerun_workflow_job and rerun_failed_workflow_run_jobs, not a general arbitrary pipeline-dispatch capability.
This mapping must not be used as a deployment shortcut even when the rerun provider action happens to execute a deployment job.

input_translation: Use repo_full_name plus run_id to enumerate workflow-run artifacts; use artifact_id only after it was observed under the bound repository/run context.
Treat optional artifact-name filtering as a provider query detail, not canonical artifact identity by itself.
output_translation: Translate provider artifact metadata/file references into bounded artifact evidence while preserving repository/run/artifact provider identities and provenance.
A downloaded artifact ZIP/file reference is evidence material; it does not by itself prove immutable digest, provenance attestation, release eligibility, or deployment.
artifact.inspect.auth_scope: Require live connector read availability for workflow artifacts. Preserve auth/scope evidence separately from domain acceptance.
artifact.inspect.verification: READ operation; bind artifact observations to the exact repository/run/provider source. Downstream digest/provenance verification remains the owning workflow's declared proof obligation when the provider output does not expose it.
artifact.inspect.sensitive_data: Artifacts may contain sensitive project data. Retrieve only authorized bounded artifacts, preserve retention/handling limits, and never copy credential/secret values into capability-resolution or Integration Result metadata.
limitations: fetch_workflow_run_artifacts returns the first page only.
download_workflow_artifact returns a reusable ZIP file reference after following the provider redirect; it is a retrieval mechanism, not artifact publication or provenance attestation.
The inspected connector surface does not provide artifact.publish.

unsupported_capabilities.pipeline.inspect_policy: No inspected GitHub connector action exposes environment protection, runner policy, concurrency policy, or required-check provider settings. Return PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED for this source rather than inferring provider-side policy from repository workflow files.
unsupported_capabilities.pipeline.update_policy: No inspected GitHub connector action mutates provider-side environment/pipeline policy. Do not invent a raw API/shell fallback without a separately authorized provider mapping revision.
unsupported_capabilities.artifact.publish: The inspected connector can list/download workflow artifacts but exposes no canonical artifact publication/promotion action. Read support must not be upgraded into write support.

failure_model.provider_absent: UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER or resolver PARTIAL/BLOCKED according to approved fallback authority; do not silently substitute another provider/source.
failure_model.authorization_denied: Preserve DENIED auth/scope evidence; do not reinterpret it as operation-policy denial or request broader credentials automatically.
failure_model.partial_capability: Return PARTIAL when the requested semantic fidelity needs an unsupported action or complete pagination that the connector wrapper does not expose.
failure_model.stale_schema: Live action discovery wins over remembered action names/schemas. A previously documented action that is absent now is unsupported for this provider source revision.
failure_model.ambiguous_write: Reconcile observed provider state before retry. Provider acknowledgement, timeout, or transport failure is not enough to claim APPLIED or no-op.
failure_model.rate_limit: Respect rate-limit/retry metadata when surfaced by the provider connector. Exact limits are unknown unless live evidence exposes them; do not hard-code guessed values.

sensitive_data_rules: Never store passwords, tokens, private keys, session secrets, or credential values in capability-resolution records, operation envelopes, Integration Result manifests, logs copied into work artifacts, or provider mapping evidence.
Treat retrieved logs and artifact files as bounded provider evidence subject to the target project's retention and privacy rules.
forbidden_ownership: technical architecture decisions outside provider translation
mapping_rule: GitHub Actions connector actions provide execution mechanics only after live discovery and capability resolution. Domain Skills own pipeline design/implementation, release readiness, and deployment decisions. Preserve provider-source identity, canonical side-effect class, operation authority, postcondition verification, partial support, and result provenance; never treat connector availability as permission or GitHub action names as canonical capabilities.
